---
title: "RESOLVE App"
---

Predict a vegetation plot's EUNIS habitat, altitude, slope, plot area, survey
year and location from the species recorded on it, with the released models
trained on the European Vegetation Archive's plots. The models run in your
browser: your files are read inside this tab and are not uploaded anywhere.
The page downloads the models and the elevation model from Zenodo
([models](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24077609),
[elevation model](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24075925)), the map from
OpenStreetMap and, for a map download, the country boundaries from Eurostat
GISCO.

```{=html}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/leaflet/1.9.4/leaflet.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../app/app.css">
<div id="resolve-app"
     data-models-pack="https://zenodo.org/api/records/24077609/files/models.tar/content"
     data-models-index="https://zenodo.org/api/records/24077609/files/models.index.json/content"
     data-terrain-field="https://zenodo.org/api/records/24075925/files/terrain_field.bin/content"
     data-examples="../app/examples/">
  <div class="panel">
    <h2 id="plots">1. Your plots</h2>
    <p class="hint" id="example-note" hidden></p>
    <div class="grid">
      <div>
        <label class="file" for="species-file">Species table</label>
        <input type="file" id="species-file" accept=".csv,.tsv,.txt">
        <div class="hint">One row per species record: plot ID, species name (World Flora Online),
          and optionally cover (%), genus and family. Columns are recognised by name, Darwin Core terms included;
          change any choice below.</div>
        <div class="fields" id="species-fields"></div>
        <div class="info" id="species-info"></div>
        <div class="error" id="species-error"></div>
      </div>
      <div>
        <label class="file" for="header-file">Header table <span class="hint">(optional)</span></label>
        <input type="file" id="header-file" accept=".csv,.tsv,.txt">
        <div class="hint">One row per plot: plot ID, latitude and longitude (WGS84), and year and month
          or a date. Each variable uses the coordinates and date where the tables give them; section 2 names
          what each is predicted from. A variable the header records on some plots (survey year, coordinates,
          altitude, slope, plot area) has its gaps fitted on the plots that record it.</div>
        <div class="fields" id="header-fields"></div>
        <div class="info" id="header-info"></div>
        <div class="error" id="header-error"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <label class="hint spelling">Misspelled species names: read as the nearest known name within
      <select id="o-spelling">
        <option value="0">no edits (names as written)</option>
        <option value="1" selected>1 edit</option>
        <option value="2">2 edits (can also rename species the models never saw)</option>
      </select></label>
    <button type="button" class="link" id="reset-data" hidden>Use the example data again</button>
  </div>

  <div class="panel">
    <h2 id="models">2. Models</h2>
    <div id="targets"></div>
    <div class="actions">
      <button id="run" disabled>Predict</button>
      <label class="hint">Workers <input type="number" id="o-workers" min="1" max="16" step="1"
        aria-describedby="workers-note"></label>
      <span id="workers-note" class="hint"></span>
      <label class="hint">Weights
        <select id="o-precision">
          <option value="half" selected>half precision (half the download)</option>
          <option value="full">full precision (the engine's own)</option>
        </select></label>
      <label class="hint" id="terrain-option" hidden><input type="checkbox" id="o-terrain" checked>
        Terrain correction of altitude and slope</label>
      <span id="download-status"></span>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="panel" id="results" hidden>
    <h2 id="predictions">3. Predictions</h2>
    <div id="busy" hidden><span class="spinner" aria-hidden="true"></span><span id="busy-verb"></span>
      <progress id="busy-bar" max="1" value="0"></progress><span id="busy-share"></span></div>
    <div id="status" role="status"></div>
    <ul id="summary"></ul>
    <ul id="gaps" hidden></ul>
    <details id="unknown" hidden><summary></summary>
      <p class="hint">Names are matched exactly against the World Flora Online names the models were trained on;
        check the spelling and the accepted name of each.</p><ul></ul></details>
    <details id="moved" hidden><summary></summary>
      <p class="hint">The models know these species by the name the European Vegetation Archive resolved its records to.
        Each name is matched through EVA's own records, the synonymy of a taxonomic backbone, or its spelling,
        named beside it.</p><ul></ul></details>
    <div class="table-wrap"><table id="table"></table></div>
    <div id="table-note"></div>
    <div id="map-note"></div>
    <div id="map" hidden></div>
    <div class="actions"><button id="download" class="secondary" disabled>Download all predictions (CSV)</button>
      <button id="download-map" class="secondary" disabled>Download map (SVG)</button></div>
  </div>

  <div class="notes">
    <p>Habitat combines its five seeds by majority vote (agreement is the share of seeds naming the class);
    numeric variables by their mean and standard deviation across seeds; location by the spherical mean and the
    median distance of the seeds from it. "Species recognised" is the share of the plot's cover held by species
    the models know. A terrain-corrected altitude or slope weighs the prediction against the elevation model
    (GLO-30) at the plot and over the square kilometre around it, by the plot's location uncertainty, the seeds'
    spread and how many of its species the models know; the elevation model's own values stand beside it.</p>
    <p>Terrain values produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-30 © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space
    GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved. The organisations
    in charge of the Copernicus programme by law or by delegation do not incur any liability for any use of the
    Copernicus WorldDEM-30.</p>
  </div>
</div>
<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/leaflet/1.9.4/leaflet.min.js"></script>
<script type="module" src="../app/app.js"></script>
```
